rows.subtype: Approach: trial and error [Action]
rows.description: A toddler twists, pulls, bangs the lid on the floor and pokes at the edge of a snack box. Each action is tried for a few seconds and dropped if nothing gives.

rows.subtype: Approach: imitation [Thinking]
rows.description: Having watched father twist the lid off a tiffin box, a toddler copies the twisting wrist motion on a box of raisins, though the twist goes the wrong way and the lid does not open.

rows.subtype: Approach: frustration overriding exploring [Pitfall]
rows.description: The lid stays stuck and a toddler grows red in the face, throws the box across the room and screams. Strong feeling ends the experimenting that might have opened it.

rows.subtype: Approach: repeating what worked [Revision]
rows.description: Once, pressing the lid corner popped a box open. The toddler now presses the corner of every lid and box, and is puzzled when a screw-top bottle does not respond.

rows.subtopic: Planning a trip on a budget
rows.subtype: Approach: fixing a total budget and working backward [Thinking]
rows.description: A group of teens with a school trip fund of 3,000 rupees each subtracts fixed costs for transport and stay, and sees only about 800 remains for food and entry tickets.

rows.subtopic: Planning a trip on a budget
rows.subtype: Approach: comparing transport and stay options [Thinking]
rows.description: Students compare a sleeper train, a bus and a shared taxi for price, time and safety, and choose the train for the overnight leg while accepting slower travel to save money.

rows.subtopic: Planning a trip on a budget
rows.subtype: Approach: overpacking the itinerary [Pitfall]
rows.description: The group plans eight places in two days, then exhausted by travel time, skips half of them and pays for tickets they never use, having ignored how slow moving actually is.

rows.subtopic: Planning a trip on a budget
rows.subtype: Approach: replanning when a booking fails [Revision]
rows.description: When the planned hostel is full, the group calls two alternatives, chooses one with a parent's approval, adjusts the food budget to cover it, and updates the shared plan.

rows.subtype: Approach: contain by changing passwords and turning on two-factor login [Action]
rows.description: After a company email says an app was breached, the person changes the password on that site and on any other site where it was reused, and enables two-factor authentication. Acting at once limits further damage.

rows.subtype: Approach: contact the bank and freeze cards if financial data is affected [Action]
rows.description: Since a card number was in the leak, the person calls the bank using the number printed on the card, blocks it and asks about alerts on transactions. Using an official channel avoids a fake helpline.

rows.subtype: Approach: ignore the notice as spam [Pitfall]
rows.description: The user assumes the email is junk and deletes it. Weeks later, someone uses the leaked details for phishing calls, and the delay makes it harder to trace.

rows.subtype: Approach: report to the company and cybercrime portal when misuse appears [Revision]
rows.description: When a suspicious transaction appears, the person moves from prevention to reporting: complaint to the bank, the cybercrime portal, and the service that leaked the data, keeping screenshots. Steps shift with new evidence.

rows.subtype: Approach: refusing and explaining why [Action]
rows.description: When a friend asks to copy the maths answers, a girl says no and offers to explain the method after class instead, holding firm without ending the friendship.

rows.subtype: Approach: thinking of what the test is for [Thinking]
rows.description: A boy reasons that copying gives marks but no learning, and that he would be lost in the next chapter, so helping someone cheat does not truly help them.

rows.subtype: Approach: giving in to keep the friendship [Pitfall]
rows.description: A child shows his answers because he fears the friend will stop talking to him, and worries afterwards, since the teacher may blame both and the fear kept growing.

rows.subtype: Approach: telling the teacher when the friend will not stop [Revision]
rows.description: After saying no twice, a boy learns that the friend plans to bring a chit into the exam, so he speaks privately with the teacher, thinking that stopping a bigger problem is worth it.

rows.subtype: Approach: following a routine of daily watering [Action]
rows.description: A girl plants tulsi and marigold in old tins, and waters them each morning before school, checking the soil with a finger to see whether it is still damp.

rows.subtype: Approach: finding out what each plant needs [Thinking]
rows.description: A boy asks the nursery man and learns that chilli needs sun while mint likes shade, and decides to place pots by the window and beside the wall accordingly.

rows.subtype: Approach: overwatering out of eagerness [Pitfall]
rows.description: A child pours water on the seedlings several times a day thinking more means faster growth, and the roots rot until the leaves yellow and the plants droop.

rows.subtype: Approach: moving the pots after the leaves burn [Revision]
rows.description: When the leaves of the rose plant turn crisp in the afternoon heat, the girl shifts it to partial shade and covers the soil with dry leaves to hold moisture.

rows.subtype: Approach: breaking the project into tasks and owners [Action]
rows.description: A team building a science model lists research, materials, construction and presentation, gives each member a task that matches their strengths and sets a date for each stage.

rows.subtype: Approach: critical path thinking [Thinking]
rows.description: The leader sees that painting cannot start until the frame dries, and that testing needs a working circuit, so she starts those dependent tasks first and lets independent ones run in parallel.

rows.subtype: Approach: doing everything alone [Pitfall]
rows.description: Not trusting others, the leader does most work at night and gets exhausted. The team feels sidelined, the quality drops, and members learn nothing from the project.

rows.subtype: Approach: inviting dissent and choosing by criteria [Revision]
rows.description: After the failure, the leader asks each member to state one concern and scores ideas on cost, time and feasibility, so the next decision uses evidence rather than confidence.
